With copper theft surging, King County prosecutor wants lawmakers to make selling it harder

Actual Article Body:
The King County Prosecutor’s Office has a plan to crack down on copper wire theft.

The office is asking the Washington state Legislature to draft a solution into law next year.

The high price of copper has made it more lucrative to steal, so public officials want to make stolen copper harder to sell.

Currently, there’s not much paperwork if sellers want to offload a box of copper odds and ends to a recycler.

But under the Prosecutor’s Office’s proposal, recyclers would have to take a photo of sellers, their copper, and their IDs.

“Then, there is a database online that these entities upload this data into, that’s searchable by law enforcement,” explained attorney Gary Ernsdorff at a press conference Monday.

If there’s a burglary report, a detective can use that database to try to find the goods and the thieves.

An interstate lawyer has been selected to prosecute the assault charges against Luke Gosling. (ABC News: Anzaya Karim)

Sydney-based barrister Sophie Callan SC has been appointed to prosecute assault charges against federal Labor MP Luke Gosling.

Mr Gosling is charged with two counts of assaulting the king's representative in the Northern Territory, and breaching his bail.

Mr Gosling denies all charges and his matter is expected to return to Darwin Local Court tomorrow.

The Northern Territory Director of Public Prosecutions (NTDPP) has engaged an interstate lawyer to take on the assault case against federal MP Luke Gosling, to avoid a perceived conflict of interest.
